plan.summary: This 4-week block is a simple off-camp build for a beginner boxer with high sport practice and only one 45-minute S&C session each week. Week 1 establishes a baseline on the main squat pattern so later loading can stay sensible without chasing fatigue. Weeks 2-4 build lower-body power, whole-body strength, and trunk support with conservative volume so sparring and boxing work stay the priority.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Establish a baseline, build basic strength, and keep power work crisp without creating extra soreness.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress the main strength and power work gradually while keeping volume low enough to recover around boxing.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength in place and shift more of the work toward faster, sharper outputs that support boxing.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.notes: Use a low box you can land on softly. Reset between reps and keep every jump fast and clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you do not have a safe box. Jump for height and stick the landing.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use bodyweight only and keep reps explosive.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Use this session to establish your current strength baseline. Warm up with a few easy sets, then work up to one hard set of 3-5 clean reps with strong depth and posture.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can set a sensible baseline for the next weeks.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if your available kettlebell or dumbbell is too light for a useful goblet squat test.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Keep the body straight and stop 1-2 reps before form breaks.

substitutionOptions.name: Hands-Elevated Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a bench, box, or sturdy surface to keep reps clean.

substitutionOptions.name: Dumbbell Floor Press
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if wrist position or floor setup makes push-ups awkward.

exercises.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Pull the elbow toward the hip, keep the torso still, and control the lowering phase.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you have a bench and want a more stable setup.

substitutionOptions.name: Backpack Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a loaded backpack if dumbbells are limited.

exercises.name: Front Plank
exercises.notes: Brace hard, squeeze glutes, and keep ribs down. End the hold before the lower back sags.

substitutionOptions.name: Body Saw Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use sliders or towels if you want a slightly harder trunk option.

exercises.name: Box Jump
exercises.notes: Use the same low box height as last week unless every landing was very clean. Full reset between reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Jump for height and land softly.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Stay bodyweight only and keep every rep sharp.

exercises.name: Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Use a load that leaves about 2 reps in reserve. Sit between the hips and keep the chest tall.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the heaviest clean set of 6 you complete with solid depth and control.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if your goblet load is too light.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Push the hips back, keep the dumbbells close, and stop when you lose hamstring tension or spinal position.

substitutionOptions.notes: Use one or two kettlebells if that is your main loading option.

substitutionOptions.name: Backpack Romanian Deadlift
